ASCENDRA

Three minds, one shared vision. We look beyond what was left behind to uncover the stories, achievements, and legacy of humanity's exploration of space. Because every mission leaves something worth remembering.

summary:
THE SILENT EXPLORERS is an interactive educational web experience that tells the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments left across the Moon, Mars and deep space. It explores how machines that have completed their missions, become inactive or continued travelling have contributed to humanity's understanding of the universe.

Organised into seven chapters, the project transforms space history into an engaging journey through storytelling, authentic NASA photographs, interactive 3D spacecraft models, narrated experiences, mission timelines and educational activities.

Developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the website integrates NASA's Image and Video Library API for discovering mission photographs and uses Google's model-viewer component to display GLB-format 3D models. It also features a searchable Mission Atlas and an Explorer Constellation where visitors collect stars and earn milestone badges as they complete chapters.

The project uses resources from NASA's Image and Video Library, NASA 3D Resources, NASA Science, the National Space Science Data Center and other credited sources. It is deployed through Netlify, making the experience accessible online.

Our mission is to make space science engaging for students while preserving the stories and scientific legacies of humanity's robotic explorers.
details:
THE SILENT EXPLORERS is an interactive educational web experience that brings the stories of humanity's robotic explorers back to life. It focuses on spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments left on the Moon, Mars and throughout deep space. The project explores what these machines were designed to do, what they discovered and how their scientific contributions continue to influence our understanding of the universe.

What does it do and how does it work?

The website takes visitors on a seven-chapter journey through space exploration. Each chapter combines scientific explanations, storytelling, NASA photographs, narrated scenes, interactive 3D models, mission timelines and educational activities.

Visitors can explore spacecraft models by rotating and zooming, discover mission photographs through NASA's Image and Video Library API, and investigate additional missions through the Mission Atlas. An Explorer Constellation allows visitors to collect stars and unlock milestone badges as they complete chapters.

What benefits does it have?

The project makes complex space science more accessible and engaging, particularly for school students. It encourages independent exploration, improves awareness of historical space missions and introduces scientific concepts through interactive experiences rather than conventional text-based learning.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and explorers. We want visitors to understand that even when a spacecraft becomes inactive or completes its mission, its discoveries and engineering legacy can continue benefiting humanity. The project also encourages appreciation of Earth's uniqueness and the importance of scientific exploration.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. NASA's Image and Video Library API provides access to mission photographs, while NASA's 3D Resources collection supplies GLB models. Google's model-viewer component, delivered through jsDelivr, enables browser-based 3D visualisation. The Web Speech API provides narration, JavaScript manages interactions and progress tracking, and Netlify hosts the finished website. Additional research resources include NASA Science, the NASA National Space Science Data Center and NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio.

How is the project creative?

Our creativity lies in transforming space hardware into an interconnected storytelling experience. Instead of simply listing technical specifications, we present missions through a cinematic seven-chapter narrative. Real space imagery, interactive 3D exploration, narration, science activities and the collectible constellation combine education with discovery and engagement.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered scientific accuracy, educational value, accessibility, ease of navigation, visual engagement, performance and reliability. We distinguished between inactive spacecraft, completed missions and spacecraft still operating or travelling. We also considered unreliable internet connections, external image availability, browser audio restrictions, loading performance and proper source attribution.
